title: The Disaster Management (Amendment) Act, 2026 (Act No. 2 of 2026)
text:
Supplement  to  the  Republic  of  Zambia  Government
Gazette  dated  Wednesday,  8th  April,  2026

[No.  2  of  2026   37

GOVERNMENT  OF  ZAMBIA

ACT

No.  2  of  2026

Date of Assent: 31st March, 2026

An Act  to  amend  the  Disaster  Management Act.

ENACTED by the Parliament of Zambia.

[8th April, 2026

1. This  Act  may  be  cited  as  the  Disaster  Management
(Amendment) Act, 2026, and shall be read as one with the Disaster
Management Act, in this Act referred to as the principal Act.

2. Section 2 of the principal Act is amended by the—

(a) deletion of the—

(i) definition of “Unit”; and

“adaptation” has the meaning assigned to the

“Division” means the National Disaster Risk

under section 4;

“disaster  risk  management  plan”  means  a
plan for disaster prevention, mitigation,
preparedness, response  and recovery;
“National  Disaster  Risk  Management
Structure” means a structure designed
to minimise the impact of a disaster by
integrating  prevention,  mitigation,
preparedness,  response  and  recovery
efforts which involves an institutional
framework consisting of the Technical
Committee,    Provincial  Committee,
District  Committee  and  Satellite
Committee;

3. The principal Act is amended in Part II by the repeal of the

heading  and the substitution therefor of the following:

PART  II
THE NATIONAL DISASTER RISK MANAGEMENT DIVISION
The principal Act is amended by the repeal of section 4

4.

and the substitution therefor of the  following:

4. There is established the National Disaster Risk
Management  Division  in  the  Office  of  the  Vice-
President,  which  shall  be  responsible  for  the
implementation of the provisions of this Act.

5. The principal Act is amended by the repeal of section 5 and

the substitution therefor of the following:

5. (1) The  Division  shall  be  responsible  for
implementing disaster risk management programmes
and activities in the Republic.

(2) Despite the generality of subsection (1),

the functions of the Division  are to—

Functions  of

(a) act as the central  planning, coordinating
and monitoring institution, taking into
account potential  disaster risks, for—
(i) the prevention and mitigation of a

disaster;

(ii) the preparedness and response to a

disaster; and

(iii) post-disaster recovery;

(b)  advise  the  Technical  Committee  on
matters  relating  to  disaster  risk
management  and  management  of
disaster relief operations;

(c) warn the public of an imminent disaster
and predict the effects of the disaster;

  40 No. 2 of 2026]          Disaster Management (Amendment)

(d)  maintain  a  data  collection  and
dissemination system,  national strategic
reserves of essential  commodities and
equipment, for purposes of immediate
disaster relief;

(e)  formulate  disaster  prevention,
mitigation,  preparedness,  response
and rehabilitation strategies and action
plans to meet  foreseeablere quirements
in  collaboration  with  Government
agencies, non-governmental organisations,
donor agencies  and  other  cooperating
partners;

(f)  prepare  and  update  disaster  risk
management plans and the supporting
disaster risk management manual;
(g) prepare an over-arching national disaster
contingency plan and coordinate cross
sectoral  disaster contingency plans;

(h)  establish  an  early  warning  system
covering all sectors and hazard sources
and maintain close links with different
institutions that provide early warning
services;

(i) develop and sustain viable and effective
structures  and  capacities  at  national,
provincial, district and satellite level;

(j)take  necessary  measures  in  order  to
prevent, alleviate, contain and minimise
the effects of a disaster;

(k) conduct public and media  briefings on
risks and disaster related programmes,
progress and constraints;

(l) act as an advisory and consultative body
on  issues  relating  to  disasters  and
disaster  risk management;

(m)  develop  post-disaster  reconstruction,
rehabilitation  and  recovery  plans  in
collaboration with relevant stakeholders;
(n)  promote  the  recruitment,  training  and
participation of volunteers in disaster
risk management;

 Disaster  Management  (Amendment)

             [No. 2 of 2026 41

(o)  establish  and  manage  a  national
emergency  operations  centre,  which
shall be—
(i) the nerve centre to monitor hazards,
risks and emergencies; and
(ii) linked to the normal operations of

the Division;

(p)  act  as  a  central  clearing  house  for  the
reporting of a disaster and dissemination
of  information  from  the  Council  and
Technical  Committee  before,  during
and after a disaster;

(q) conduct comprehensive vulnerability and
risk  assessments  before,  during  and
after a disaster;

(r)  collaborate  with  other  institutions  and
organisations which are responsible for
disaster risk management at national,
regional and international level;
(s) promote the integration of disaster risk
reduction  and  climate  change
adaptation for purposes of enhancing
capacities and strengthening resilience
of communities; and

(t) maintain,  and  cause  to  be  maintained,
adequate  response  capacity  and
equipment to facilitate timely, effective
and  efficient  response  to  a  recurrent
and anticipated disaster including—
(i)  ground  and  aerial  assessment  and
analysis tools for capturing spatial
and digital data and images;
(ii) ground and aerial transportation and
haulage equipment sufficient for
timely and  efficient dispatch of
supplies  to  a  disaster  affected
area;

(iii)  ground  and  aerial  transportation
equipment for timely and efficient
dispatch of emergency response
teams, equipment and materials;

  42 No. 2 of 2026]          Disaster Management (Amendment)

(iv)  warehousing  infrastructure,
equipment and tools which enable
timely  receipt,  organisation,
documentation  and  dispatch  of
relief supplies; and

(v) equipment and tools for emergency
reconstruction and rehabilitation of
a disaster affected infrastructure.
(3) The  functions  of  the  Division    shall  be
guided by the humanitarian principle of do no harm.
(4) The Division shall be the secretariat to the

National Disaster Risk Management Structure.

of section 7

6. Section 7 of the principal Act is amended by the deletion of

subsection (3) and the substitution therefor of the following:

(3) The Division shall—

(a) monitor—

(i) progress with the preparation, and regular update,
of disaster risk management plans and business
continuity  plans  by  a  person,  institution  or
organisation  involved  in  disaster  risk
management; and

(ii) formal and informal prevention, mitigation and
response initiatives by Government departments
and  ministries,  the  private  sector,  non-
governmental organisations and communities,
including the integration of the initiatives with
development risk plans; and

11. Section 13 of the principal Act is amended by the deletion

of subsection (5) and the substitution therefor of the following:

(5) The Civil Service Commission shall

(j)   proposed addresses,  locations and coordinates

15.

The principal Act is amended by the repeal of section

19 and the substitution therefor of the following:

19. (1) The  Civil  Service  Commission  shall
appoint, as a public officer, a Provincial Disaster Risk
Management Coordinator.

(2) The Provincial Disaster Risk Management
Coordinator shall provide technical advisory support
to a Provincial Committee,  District Committee and
Satellite Committee.

16. The principal Act is amended in Part IV by the deletion of

the heading and the substitution therefor of the following:

PART  IV
DISTRICT AND SATELLITE DISASTER RISK
MANAGEMENT COMMITTEES

17. Section 21 of the principal Act is amended by the deletion

of —

(a) subsection (1) and the substitution therefor of the following:
(1)  There  is  constituted a    District  Disaster
Risk Management Committee in each district which
shall be a sub-committee of the District Development
Coordinating Committee.;

(b) subsection (2) and the substitution  therefor of the following:
(2) A  District  Committee  consists  of  the
following  part-time    members  appointed  by  the
Provincial Permanent Secretary:

(a)  the  District  Commissioner,  as  the

Chairperson;

(b)  seven  representatives    of  Government

departments in the district;

(c) Members of Parliament in the district;
(d) a representative of the Zambia Red Cross

Society;

(e)  a  representative  each  of  the  non-
governmental  organisations  and
community-based organisations involved
in disaster management in the district;

in the district; and

(g) one person from the private sector with
relevant knowledge and experience in
matters relating to this Act; and

(c) subsection (3) and the substitution therefor of the following:
(3) The  District  Disaster  Risk
Management  Co-ordinator  shall  be    the
secretary of the District Committee.

in  consultation  with  the  Division,  Zambia  Police
Service,  national  security  services  and  any  other
institution involved in disaster risk management in the
district.

(a) the insertion of the following new  subsections immediately

after subsection (1):
